title: Harvesting Murine Alveolar Macrophages and Evaluating Cellular Activation Induced by Polyanhydride Nanoparticles
protocol: Wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE).
Prepare complete AMɸ medium before initiation of harvest.
Add 2.5 mL of penicillin/streptomycin solution to the medium.
Add 250 μL of β-mercaptoethanol to the medium.
Add 25 mL of heat inactivated fetal bovine serum (FBS) to the medium.
Filter-sterilize cAMɸ medium using a 0.2 μm pore size bottle top filter under vacuum.
Euthanize a healthy mouse by CO2 asphyxiation in an euthanization chamber.
Place the mouse in the chamber for at least one minute to ensure euthanasia.
Exsanguinate each mouse via cardiac puncture to confirm death.
Lay mouse on its back (dorsal side).
Spray mouse with 70% ethanol.
Locate the sternum and, at a 30 degree angle from the abdomen, insert a 23 gauge needle about 50 mm into the thoracic cavity to collect blood.
Examine the animal for cessation of vital signs.
Place mouse on lab bench so that it is lying on its abdomen (ventral side).
Spray mouse with 70% ethanol to sterilize the working environment.
Pinch skin about halfway down the spine of the mouse.
Using dissection scissors, make a small incision through the skin and pull the skin in opposite directions along the cranial-caudal axis to remove skin from underlying carcass.
Carefully cut tissue and pull it towards the anterior of the mouse using forceps to expose the larynx, trachea, and esophagus.
Hold the trachea with forceps and gently lift and separate the trachea from the esophagus.
Make a small incision anterior to the trachea but posterior to the larynx at approximately a 45° angle.
Hold the trachea using forceps.
Fill a 1 cc syringe fitted with a Tom Cat catheter with sterile PBS.
Gently insert the catheter into the tracheal incision site about 20 mm.
Infuse 0.75 mL of room temperature, sterile PBS into the lungs through the catheter.
Gently aspirate the PBS back into the syringe.
Externally massage the chest to aid in fluid circulation.
Repeat steps involving infusion and aspiration three times.
Disconnect the syringe from the catheter after completing infusions and aspirations.
Dispense the lavage fluid into a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge lung lavage fluid at 250 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Using sterile technique, decant supernatant into appropriate waste container inside a biosafety cabinet.
Resuspend the cell pellet by gently raking the centrifuge tube across the top of a test tube rack.
Add 1 mL of cAMɸ medium to resuspend the cells.
Pipette 20 μL of cells into 10 mL of Isoton II Diluent in Coulter counter vial.
Add 3 to 4 drops of Zap-oglobin II lytic reagent into vial and gently invert 3 to 4 times.
Load the sample vial onto the Coulter Particle Counter Z1.
Program the counter with a dilution factor of 2 x 10^4 to display the cell concentration as the number of cells per mL.
Dilute cells to 2.5 x 10^5 per mL using cAMɸ medium.
Dispense 2 mL of 2.5 x 10^5 cells/mL into each well of a 6-well tissue culture dish.
Incubate culture dishes inside a 37 °C humidified incubator with a 5% CO2 atmosphere for 6 h to allow cells to adhere to the bottom of the well.
Gently aspirate the supernatant as to not disrupt adherent cells.
Rinse the wells using sterile PBS (calcium and magnesium free) to remove non-adherent cells and debris.
Add 2 mL of cAMɸ medium to each well.
Incubate cells overnight inside a 37 °C humidified incubator with a 5% CO2 atmosphere prior to addition of stimulants.
Fabricate nanoparticles via polyanhydride anti-solvent nanoencapsulation.
Dissolve the polymer in methylene chloride at 4 °C with a concentration of 25 mg/mL.
Precipitate the solution in pentane at -20 °C using a ratio of 1:200 methylene chloride:pentane.
Weigh out polyanhydride nanoparticles using sterilized weigh paper on an accurate microgram balance.
Add particles to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Resuspend the nanoparticles in ice cold cAMɸ.
Keep the resuspended particles on ice until adding to the culture well.
Sterilize microtip by spraying with 70% ethanol and wiping with a sterile Kimwipe.
Sonicate particles at 10-20 joules for 30 to 45 seconds while keeping the tube on ice.
Observe nanoparticle suspension macroscopically.
If particles are not sufficiently dispersed, allow the suspension to set on ice for 1 to 2 minutes before sonicating again for 30 to 45 seconds.
Keep the adequately dispersed nanoparticle suspension on ice and use immediately.
Remove culture dishes containing the AMɸ from the incubator and place them in the biosafety cabinet.
Tilt the plates at approximately a 45-degree angle.
Pipette off the medium amount that will be added to the nanoparticle suspension, ensuring it does not exceed 0.3 mL.
Vortex the polyanhydride nanoparticle suspension briefly before use.
Pipette no more than 0.3 mL of nanoparticle suspension into the specific well(s).
Avoid pipetting up and down to mix; this could detach adherent AMɸ from the well.
Proceed with subsequent wells and desired treatment groups, including positive and negative control groups such as medium only and 200 ng/mL lipopolysaccharide (LPS).
Return the culture dishes to the 37 °C humidified incubator.
Maintain a 5% CO2 atmosphere for the incubation period.
Incubate the cultures for 48 hours.
Prepare FACS buffer by adding 0.1% sodium azide and 0.1% bovine serum albumin (BSA) to 0.1 M phosphate buffered saline (pH 7.4).
Dilute rat IgG (Sigma) to 1 mg/mL in FACS buffer.
Dilute anti-CD16/32 (eBioscience) to 10 μg/mL in FACS buffer.
Prepare surface marker antibody panel by diluting antibodies against MHC II, CD86, CD40, and CIRE (CD209) in FACS buffer at the manufacturer's recommended or user-optimized concentration.
Place cell culture dishes on ice for 20 min after 48 h of incubation with nanoparticles and/or stimulants.
Gently scrape wells with a 24 cm cell scraper to remove adherent macrophages.
Using a 5 mL serological pipette, gently aspirate the cells and medium up and down five times to generate a single cell suspension.
Pipette the contents of individual wells into separate 5 mL polystyrene tubes so as not to mix together cells from different experimental treatments.
Add 2 mL of FACS buffer to each tube.
Centrifuge tubes of cells at 250 x g at 4 °C for 10 min.
Decant supernatant.
Gently resuspend cell pellet in residual fluid by raking the tubes across the top of a test tube rack.
Add 10 μL of blocking buffer to each tube of cells.
Vortex tubes and incubate on ice for 30 min.
Add appropriate volume of diluted monoclonal antibodies to each tube.
Incubate in the dark on ice for 15 min.
Include a tube of unlabeled cells as an additional control group.
Prepare compensation tubes using labeled cells with each single color separately.
Include Fluorescence Minus One (FMO) controls during acquisition.
Add positive and negative population samples to FMO and compensation control tubes.
Add 2 mL of FACS buffer to each tube.
Vortex tubes and centrifuge at 250 x g at 4 °C for 10 min.
Decant supernatant from each tube.
Resuspend cell pellet in residual fluid by raking the tubes across a test tube rack.
Dilute an appropriate volume of BD stabilizing fixative 1:3 in deionized water.
Add 100 μl of diluted fixative to each tube while gently vortexing to prevent clumping of cells.
Store labeled and fixed cells in the dark at 4°C for approximately one week prior to acquisition on a flow cytometer.
